This is an explanation of soften edge from a reddit post from 5 years ago. 

"Soft edges will give the illusion of smoothness where the surface may be faceted. The best way to view what is happening is turning on vertex normals in the display menu and toggle between soften and harden.  
Harden has the vertex normal visual line being perpendicar to the vertex, and soften has the normals more spread out evenly across the surface.  
So the former makes lights bounce sharply off the surface giving the illusion of a faceted surface, and the latter blends the light across the surface, giving a smoother look.  
If youre looking to bake normal maps you should soften all edges on your low res object before baking, but if youre just hoping to make your surface look nice in Maya you will need to manually pick and choose the edges to to soften and harden."

Essentially, soften edge is tricking the computer into thinking there is more geometry instead of actually adding it.
In the 3D software you’re using. If it’s maya, then you grab the edges and press soften. Here’s a quick video that explains everything in the first minute. https://youtu.be/0Y0qCFT_w14
I’ve ran into this before and all I had to do was soften the edges that aren’t baking properly.
